req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid URL
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter of /redirect-to is missing or malformed.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must return HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter is missing or malformed. Examining the source code (lines 572-644), the handler does `response.headers['Location'] = args['url'].encode('utf-8')` — if 'url' is absent, a KeyError is raised (no explicit 400 guard exists in the shown source). This means the current implementation may not actually return 400 for missing url (it raises an unhandled KeyError, which Flask converts to 500), making this a specification vs. implementation gap. Tests must probe: (1) valid url present → 302/3xx redirect (positive/EP), (2) url parameter missing → 400 (negative/NEG), (3) url parameter empty string → 400 (boundary/BVA), (4) custom status_code at boundary values 300 and 399 (BVA), (5) malformed/non-URL string → 400 (NEG/DT). The tests assert exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /redirect-to is accessible via test client
trace: R-HTTPBIN-027: positive path — valid url parameter produces redirect
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302()
